**1.5h**

Today I fully designed my pcb I had some prior experience from the hack club, hackpad project which I did not complete. I was able to finish the schematic pretty quickly. After finishing that about 40% of my time was spent trying to figure out why my footprint library wasn't working. I ended up figuring it out but it did take a while.

### 2026-10-07 – ![one](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/VUsqYsJQU3oaQ5M5MTZACBI7uSlmkXMr/283d516904a22c3901fd4b281fc68a3ead6f929e0c057fab74beb42b3cb47651.jpg)

**2h**

![one](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/VUsqYsJQU3oaQ5M5MTZACBI7uSlmkXMr/283d516904a22c3901fd4b281fc68a3ead6f929e0c057fab74beb42b3cb47651.jpg)

Today I began working on my code for the macro pad. After working on that for 30 minutes, I checked in with a friend and they pointed out a flaw in my PCB design I was originally trying to save space by overlapping two of the parts/footprints, but it wasn't going to work out in the end. So they pointed that out to me, and I ended up fixing it. I also did not have a border/edge cut for my PCB, so I ended up also doing that. We also checked in about my code, and they said it looked fine to them.

**1h**

This this session, I added a silk screen dinosaur to my PCB. and uploaded started uploading the files to my GitHub repository. I had a little trouble figuring out the silk screen. I ran a DRC in Kicad and came up with several silk screen errors, so I fixed those.

### 2026-10-10 – ![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 4.01.16 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/VUsqYsJQU3oaQ5M5MTZACBI7uSlmkXMr/fd5b9a1e7e74159523878e15ab2c1849b3ff0401d0fadb0dc92e61b72c228c3

**1.5h**

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 4.01.16 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/VUsqYsJQU3oaQ5M5MTZACBI7uSlmkXMr/fd5b9a1e7e74159523878e15ab2c1849b3ff0401d0fadb0dc92e61b72c228c3c.jpg)

I thought it would be cool to add Bluetooth so I was looking originally to add a raspberry pie radio module 2 but then I realized the radio model has pads underneath the board, so it would be hard to solder after doing more research. I discovered a seeed studio XIAO-nRF52840-DIP which is a Wi-Fi and Bluetooth board? I began working on adding it to my schematic because it has the same surface area as the microcontroller I was already using, so I wouldn't have to change my PCB design, but then I realized the coding aspect of it would potentially be more complex than I was willing to adapt to.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 3.54.59 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/VUsqYsJQU3oaQ5M5MTZACBI7uSlmkXMr/272413379066de8a8ed427402c576a71025afd29ecdbe68334d7552e2dc4e1e7.jpg)
